GRU4Rec reproducibility research shows implementation differences can substantially distort accuracy and runtime; a recurrent-execution repair therefore needs its own measured baseline before testing cropping. Official documentation distinguishes session-based execution from longer user-history modeling, where backpropagation through time and history-conditioned inference matter. Audit hidden-state reset boundaries, padding effects, truncation/detachment, dropout placement and mask reuse, and train/eval behavior. For this benchmark’s left padding, read the final nonpadding position. Keep repaired execution identical across cropping conditions. [Reproducibility study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.14956), [official implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec).

Recommended ablation: corrected GRU4Rec without cropping versus the same corrected model with cropping only. Match sampled users, target positions, negatives, batch size, optimizer updates, loss normalization and checkpoint selection; crop only the preceding context while preserving target alignment and excluding future interactions. If cropping removes supervised positions, either match those positions across conditions or explicitly identify supervision quantity as another changed factor. CL4SRec supports augmentation as a research direction, but combines augmented views with an auxiliary contrastive objective; its results do not isolate supervised context cropping. Record supervised-target counts, processed tokens and GPU seconds because equal epochs alone do not establish equal supervision or compute. [CL4SRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.14395).

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four categories, 200 batches/epoch and the 200-epoch ceiling fixed. Compare macro validation HR@10 using exactly the pinned users and candidates; retain one trained checkpoint per category. Sampled ranking metrics can reverse model order relative to full-catalog evaluation, so interpret gains specifically under the fixed 99-negative protocol without changing the evaluator or claiming full-catalog improvement. [Sampled-metric analysis](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).
